claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a closely matched high-entropy derivative has a coercive field of approximately 100 Oe or less.
Thermal annealing can induce nanoscale precipitation of a chemically ordered secondary phase in an FeCoNi-based fcc matrix without changing the overall composition.
Appropriately controlled annealing can produce coherent B2 precipitates while avoiding complete or large-scale phase separation.
The intervention will form a dual-phase microstructure consisting of nanoscale coherent B2 precipitates embedded in an fcc matrix.
Nanoscale B2 precipitates will act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Pinning by the precipitates will increase resistance to domain-wall motion.
Increased resistance to domain-wall motion will increase the coercive field.
Annealed material containing the precipitates will have higher coercivity than baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative.
The coercive field after the intervention is expected to exceed approximately 100 Oe.
XRD and TEM can be used to assess the phase structure and verify nanoscale precipitates.
VSM or SQUID hysteresis measurements can determine the coercive field of control and annealed samples.
